parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.stem:
The diagram shows the apparatus used to measure the standard electrode potential, $E^{\ominus}$, of $\text{Fe}^{3+}\text{(aq)}/\text{Fe}^{2+}\text{(aq)}$.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}
parts.text: Identify what the letters **A** to **F** represent.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
Label the diagram to show

- which is the positive electrode,
- the direction of electron flow in the external circuit.

Use the *Data Booklet* to help you.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
In another experiment, an $\text{Fe}^{3+}\text{(aq)}/\text{Fe}^{2+}\text{(aq)}$ half-cell was connected to a $\text{Cu}^{2+}\text{(aq)}/\text{Cu(s)}$ half-cell.

Determine the standard cell potential, $E^{\ominus}_{\text{cell}}$, when these two half-cells are connected by a wire and the circuit is completed.

Use the *Data Booklet* to help you.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text:
The $E^{\ominus}$ of $\text{Ni}^{2+}\text{(aq)}/\text{Ni(s)}$ is $-0.25\text{ V}$.

State and explain how the electrode potential changes if the concentration of $\text{Ni}^{2+}\text{(aq)}$ is decreased.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
The $E^{\ominus}$ of $\text{Cr}^{3+}\text{(aq)}/\text{Cr}^{2+}\text{(aq)}$ is $-0.41\text{ V}$.

Calculate the electrode potential when $[\text{Cr}^{3+}\text{(aq)}]$ is $0.60\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ and $[\text{Cr}^{2+}\text{(aq)}]$ is $0.15\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$. Use the Nernst equation.

$$E = E^{\ominus} + \frac{0.059}{z} \log \frac{[\text{oxidised species}]}{[\text{reduced species}]}$$
